rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a residential unit only by consent or through court eviction, and must have good cause (statutory grounds). Each cause except nonpayment must be described in a written notice, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment; the landlord may not evict or refuse to renew a lease without good cause.
rules.key_value: Warrant for possession not issued until 3 business days after judgment; tenant has 3 business days to move
rules.status_basis: Described as existing law in the NJ DCA publication.

exempt_if.text: two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units

exempt_if.name: transient_seasonal_lodging
exempt_if.text: hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant

exempt_if.name: family_trust_unit
exempt_if.text: unit held in trust on behalf of a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rentals including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, and rooming and boarding homes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Does not apply to certain owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises, transient or seasonal guests, or a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

rules.quoted_span: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause eviction.
